status: STARTING VALUES from public trade sources. Rule-of-thumb only. Verify on the production floor and against the ink maker's technical data sheet before use.

confidence_key.sourced: Value taken from a named public source (see 'source').
confidence_key.interpolated: Value calculated between two sourced values. Not directly published.
confidence_key.assumption: No reliable public source found. Placeholder to be replaced with factory data.

units.mesh: Both US threads per inch (tpi) and metric threads per cm (t_cm). t_cm = tpi / 2.54.
units.temperature: Degrees Celsius, with Fahrenheit as published.
units.ink_deposit: Wet grams per square metre of printed (inked) area, one stroke.

mesh_rules.note: Lower mesh gives more opacity but a heavier hand feel.

mesh_rules.applies_to: General plastisol spot colours, average detail
mesh_rules.note: 156 tpi (62T) is the common all-purpose choice.
mesh_rules.changed_by_ravi: 18 Nov 2026: range 137-156 tpi (was 137-160), so every end has an ink_consumption entry

mesh_rules.note: Very low mesh lets thin water-based ink bleed; thick water-based whites for darks may run lower. Follow the ink data sheet.

mesh_rules.applies_to: Thin lines, small text (under about 10 pt), detailed logos

mesh_rules.note: Choose the exact mesh from halftone_rules using the LPI.

mesh_rules.applies_to: Heavy white, athletic numbers, metallic, thick special-effect inks, rough fabrics
mesh_rules.note: Glitter and high-density inks usually need even coarser mesh; take that value from the ink maker.

halftone_rules.formula: minimum mesh (tpi) = LPI x 4 to 5. Use 5 for a safer result.
halftone_rules.note: Sources agree on a 4x to 5x ratio. One source quotes a different ratio and is not used here.

detail_rules.note: Warn the user when a colour layer has lines thinner than the limit for its mesh.

screen_type_mesh_rule.pending: highlight_white: Ravi to give the tpi range; until then it uses halftone_simulated_process
screen_type_mesh_rule.note: Which mesh_rules entry each screen type in the Print Report uses; the report shows that entry's tpi range. Proposed 18 Nov 2026 to replace mesh numbers that were written in the Kotlin code (underbase 110, highlight white 230, CMYK 305, spot halftone 200, flat spot 156); Ravi to confirm. Ink per screen uses ink_consumption at the two ends of the range; an end with no entry there gives no figure.

underbase_rules.needed_when: Light or bright colours printed on a dark base fabric
underbase_rules.note: 0.5 mm is the published figure. The lower limit 0.2 mm is an assumption for tight-registration presses. Never choke so far that thin text loses its white base.

sequence: 3. Top colours, lower mesh before higher mesh (coarse first, fine second)
print_order_rules.note: Light-to-dark colour order within the top colours is common shop practice but was not confirmed by a source here; treat it as an assumption.

ink_systems.name: Plastisol (standard)
ink_systems.note: The whole ink film must reach cure temperature, not only the surface.

ink_systems.name: Plastisol (low-cure / low-bleed, for polyester)
ink_systems.note: Exact cure point comes from the ink data sheet. Density assumed same as standard plastisol.

ink_systems.name: Water-based pigment
ink_systems.note: Weak coverage on dark fabric without underbase or discharge. Density 1.1 is an assumption.

ink_systems.name: Discharge
ink_systems.note: Works by removing the cotton dye, so the result depends on the fabric dye being dischargeable. Time and temperature both matter. Density 1.1 is an assumption.

fabric_rules.when: Fibre is 100% polyester or a polyester blend
fabric_rules.risk: Dye migration: polyester dye moves into the ink and changes its colour, mostly whites and pastels.
actions: Use a dye-migration blocker as underbase
Cure at the lowest temperature the ink maker allows
Check the print again after 24 to 48 hours; migration can appear late

fabric_rules.when: 50/50 cotton/polyester with white or light print

actions: Underbase white with plastisol or water-based top colours
Or discharge, if the fabric dye is dischargeable

fabric_rules.source: General practice; not confirmed from a source in this research.

ink_consumption.formula: ink_g = printed_area_m2 x coverage_fraction x deposit_g_m2 x strokes x pieces x (1 + wastage_fraction)
ink_consumption.note: printed_area_m2 is the print box (width x height). coverage_fraction is that colour's share of the box. If the app already gives the colour's own area in cm2, use that and set coverage to 1.
ink_consumption.cross_check: An ink maker's sheet gives 0.02278 g per square inch at 305 mesh with double pass, which is about 35 g/m2 for two strokes, or about 18 g/m2 per stroke. This matches the 305 mesh default above.
ink_consumption.water_based_note: Published default for print paste pick-up at full coverage in textile printing. Wide range; replace with factory figures.
ink_consumption.wastage_note: No reliable public figure found. One trade example adds 5% extra. 10% is a placeholder; replace with factory data.

dye_calculator.note: Standard exhaust dyeing arithmetic (percent on weight of fabric, liquor ratio 1:n). All recipe values are entered by the user. The app never creates a recipe from an image.
dye_calculator.source: Standard textile dyeing calculation; no recipe values are included in this file.

display_disclaimer: Rule-of-thumb estimate from public trade sources. Verify on the production floor and with the ink maker's technical data sheet.
change_log: v2 (15 Nov 2026): added process_inks, garment_mask, white_base, recommendation, resolution and regression_cases after a device test on a real garment photo (white-to-blue gradient logo on a black T-shirt).

v3 (18 Nov 2026): added shadow_vs_ink and photo_vs_artwork (proposed starting values, Ravi to confirm) after a white T-shirt photo measured fold shadows as print colours. merge_shades_in_photo_hue_within_deg holds the 6 deg from merge_shades_in_photo as a number. Added edge_blend (camera blur and anti-aliasing bands between two inks; proposed starting values, Ravi to confirm). Added small_colours: a colour under the minimum coverage is flagged, not dropped (the magenta eye on the skull print). Added screen_type_mesh_rule (mesh per screen type from mesh_rules; ink figures only where ink_consumption has an entry). Ravi: flat spot 137-156 tpi; mapping verified except highlight white. Added artwork_background. Added edge_blend.keyline_protection (Ravi: black keylines are important) and photo_background (table or floor at the photo edge). Added garment_preview (contrast check and preview chips). Added print_brief (feel tags from the technique texts, method order) and quantity_thresholds (values empty until Ravi gives them). Added mixed_separation (CMYK plus spot screens for solid colours; black text from the K screen). Ravi 19 Nov: quantity is the buyer's order and does not change the method (quantity_changes_method false).

process_inks.note: Nominal screen colours for the model only. Replace with the ink maker's measured values. Offer CMYK process only on white or light garments, or over a white base.

garment_mask.estimate_from: median Lab of the image border region; user 'tap the fabric' overrides; presets are only an initial guess
garment_mask.note: A photo never shows fabric as one pure colour: black fabric measured L* 9 to 30 in the device test. Never assume #000000 or #FFFFFF. All numbers here are starting values to tune on real garment photos.

white_base.needed_when: garment L* below 70, or garment chroma above 15, and the print has colours lighter or brighter than the garment
white_base.area: only under print pixels, never under bare fabric
white_base.highlight_white: only the brightest highlights above an adjustable threshold
white_base.user_switch: 'Use white base' overrides the automatic decision
white_base.floor_confirmation: Ravi confirmed on 15 Nov 2026 that a white + blue gradient logo on black prints as white solid with blue halftone over it: 2 screens, or 3 if a separate base is flashed first.
white_base.note: The lightness and chroma limits are placeholders. Mid-tone garments (red, grey) also need a base for many colours.

ink_model.light_garment: transparent ink (absorbance) model: darker pixel means more ink
ink_model.dark_or_coloured_garment: opaque ink over garment: pixel = (1 - coverage) x garment + coverage x ink, in linear RGB. A pixel equal to the garment has zero ink on every screen.
ink_model.never: Never create a screen whose ink is the garment colour (for example black ink on a black garment).
ink_model.note: Model choice follows the white_base rule. Both models ignore dot gain and registration.

recommendation.principle: Recommend the option with the fewest screens that meets the quality tolerance, not the option with the lowest colour error.
recommendation.start_from: one spot ink per colour family of print colours
recommendation.gradient_rule: A smooth transition between two inks is reported as 'ink A as halftone over ink B' and counts as 2 screens.
recommendation.offer_cmyk_when: artwork is tonal with at least 4 distinct hue families, on a white or light garment or over a white base
recommendation.user_choice: The user can always pick another option. Show the reason for the recommendation in one line.
recommendation.note: Tolerances are placeholders aligned with the shade match grades (below 2 good, 2 to 4 visible). Tune with real jobs.

resolution.equivalent_dpi: 59 px/cm is about 150 dpi; 118 px/cm is about 300 dpi at print size
resolution.below_min_action: Warn that fine lines and small text cannot be trusted; suggest retaking closer so the print fills the frame.
resolution.edge_refinement: For flat spot layers only: upsample, smooth, re-threshold. Deterministic.
resolution.never: No AI or generative upscaling in any measurement.
resolution.note: 300 dpi at print size is common artwork practice; it was not verified from a source in this research.

shadow_vs_ink.edge_width_measure: distance over which lightness moves from 10% to 90% of the step, in mm at print scale
shadow_vs_ink.uncertain_action: keep as a colour, label 'Possible fold shadow - tap to confirm', show screens as 'N (+1 if this is ink)'
shadow_vs_ink.note: Proposed starting values; tune on real photos; Ravi to confirm

photo_vs_artwork.merge_shades_in_photo: same hue within 6 deg and lightness change smooth across a connected region
photo_vs_artwork.merge_shades_in_photo_smooth_means: the lightness change across the border between the two shades is wider than shadow_vs_ink.ink_edge_max_mm (not a stencil edge); neutral shades (chroma below shadow_vs_ink.hue_test_only_if_garment_chroma_at_least) have no reliable hue and are not merged
photo_vs_artwork.merge_shades_in_artwork: never automatic; if the lighter shade fits the garment-to-ink mixing line within 2.0 CIEDE2000, suggest 'print as tint of <ink>, saves 1 screen' for the user to accept
photo_vs_artwork.note: Proposed starting values; tune on real photos; Ravi to confirm

photo_background.what: table, floor or wall at the edge of a garment photo: not fabric and not print
photo_background.region_is_background_if: a non-fabric region touches the photo border along at least min_border_touch_fraction of one side, covers at least min_area_percent of the photo, and does not reach the centre box (the middle centre_box_fraction of the width and of the height)
photo_background.action: exclude from the print; show it shaded in the mask picture; the switch 'Include the photo edge area' undoes it
photo_background.capture_guidance: Fill the frame with the garment. Nothing else in the photo.
photo_background.note: Proposed starting values; Ravi to confirm. The centre-box condition keeps a large print that runs off one edge.

mixed_separation.what: CMYK halftone for the picture plus spot screens for solid colours (text, logos). A near-black solid colour prints from the K screen, so it needs no extra screen.
mixed_separation.offered_when: CMYK is offered (recommendation.cmyk_min_hue_families) and at least one print colour is solid while others are tonal
mixed_separation.solid_rule: A print colour is solid when at least solid_min_share of the pixels nearest to it are within solid_core_de00 of it. Pixels within solid_core_de00 of a solid colour print from its spot screen; all other print pixels print from C, M, Y and K.
mixed_separation.black_rule: A solid colour within black_from_k_max_de00 of the process black (process_inks.black) prints from the K screen instead of its own screen.
mixed_separation.prefer_reason: Small solid text built from C, M, Y and K risks misregistration, and the colour-error figures do not include registration. So when CMYK would be recommended and the mixed option is within tolerance (or nothing is), the mixed option is recommended.
mixed_separation.note: Proposed 19 Nov 2026; all three numbers are starting values. Ravi to confirm.

print_brief.what: Four tap questions (garment colour, fibre and fabric, quantity, feel) and one decision card
print_brief.fabric_note: The fabric is shown on the card and passed to the AI explanation. No rule in this file uses it yet.
print_brief.feel_source: Taken from each technique's own text in print_techniques.json (water-based: soft, breathable feel; discharge: very soft print; plastisol: slightly raised plastic feel). Techniques not listed have no feel tag and are neutral.
print_brief.method_order: A method ruled out by fibre, artwork or garment is never offered. The rest are ordered by: matches the quantity band, then matches the feel, then the chosen fibre is listed as suitable (listed, then no fibre data, then not listed), then verified by Ravi, then advice level (recommended before possible), then fewer cautions (a caution warns of a weakness; a note only states a condition), then file order.
print_brief.note: Proposed 18 Nov 2026; Ravi to confirm the feel tags and the method order.

quantity_thresholds.what: Order quantity and the print method
quantity_thresholds.rule: The order quantity is the buyer's order. It does not change the method; it is used for the ink totals of the order. The two limits stay empty while quantity_changes_method is false.

garment_preview.what: 'See it on your garment': the print drawn on a chosen garment colour, on the phone
garment_preview.model: without a white base: transparent ink over the garment (ink_model.light_garment); with a white base: ink over white. No ink opacity value is used because the rules file has none; this is a model preview, not a proof
garment_preview.chips_note: Taken from the Print Report garment chips. The Artwork Preview screen uses #0B1020 for navy; Ravi to choose one
garment_preview.contrast_rule: an ink whose lightness differs from the garment's by less than contrast_min_delta_L is hard to see; warn and offer a one-tap swap
garment_preview.note: Proposed 18 Nov 2026; the contrast limit 30 and the cream colour are starting values; Ravi to confirm.

artwork_background.what: the plain background of an artwork file (paper, canvas colour): not ink unless the user says to print it
artwork_background.rule: a colour is background when at least border_share_min of the border pixels are within the fabric threshold of it and the border is flat (spread at most flat_spread_max_de00)
artwork_background.action: ask 'This looks like background, not ink. Print it or drop it?'; until answered it is left out (not ink); if printed it counts in colours, screens, ink and coverage
artwork_background.garment: the garment colour of an artwork file is never taken from the background or the AI read; the user chooses it
artwork_background.also_for_photos: when one colour holds at least border_share_min of the border of a garment photo, that colour is the fabric even if it differs from the garment preset (a pink jersey is not white)
artwork_background.note: Proposed starting values 18 Nov 2026; Ravi to confirm.

small_colours.real_ink_if: at least one connected region of that colour with area >= min_region_mm2 at print scale, and CIEDE2000 from every palette colour >= the merge threshold
small_colours.merge_threshold_note: the CIEDE2000 limit Part A already uses to merge near-identical clusters (step 8)
small_colours.flag_text: Small colour, about N%: confirm it is an ink
small_colours.noise_if: only scattered regions each smaller than min_region_mm2
small_colours.noise_action: remove, and show 'N speck pixels removed'
small_colours.note: Proposed starting values; Ravi to confirm. A small accent colour is still a screen unless the merchandiser drops it. min_coverage_percent and merge_threshold_de00 were constants in the Part A code before 18 Nov 2026.

edge_blend.what: thin bands of mixed colour along the border between two inks (or ink and fabric), from camera blur or artwork anti-aliasing; not an ink
edge_blend.band_width: measured in the analysed image, not the source
edge_blend.blur_measured_from: 10-90% width of clean ink-to-fabric edges in the same image
edge_blend.sandwiched_means: both neighbouring colours within the band width of the pixel
edge_blend.plateau_keep_rule: keep as a colour if, across the band, at least 2 consecutive pixels have the same mixing ratio within 0.1 (a printed line has a flat middle; blur does not)

keyline_protection.rule: a thin band much darker than both neighbours (lightness below both neighbouring colours by at least keyline_min_L_drop) is a keyline, never blur, whatever its width
keyline_protection.applies_to: black and any dark line colour; also any band that fails the colour-family test
keyline_protection.floor_confirmation: Ravi confirmed 18 Nov 2026 that black keylines are common and important

edge_blend.action_photo: reassign each blend pixel to the nearer neighbour by mixing ratio; a pixel nearer the fabric leaves the print area
edge_blend.action_artwork: same, only when the band is band_max_px_artwork or thinner (anti-aliasing); otherwise keep the colour
edge_blend.if_line_but_not_thin: keep as a colour (may be a real tint or gradient)
edge_blend.below_min_px_per_cm: flag 'possible thin line or blur - confirm' instead of merging
edge_blend.report: show count of reassigned pixels; switch 'Keep edge colours as separate inks' undoes it
edge_blend.note: Proposed starting values; tune on real photos; Ravi to confirm. plateau_min_px and plateau_ratio_tolerance hold the 2 and 0.1 from plateau_keep_rule as numbers.

regression_cases.description: Photo of a dark textured garment with uneven lighting; one solid white logo with a blue gradient fading over its top part.
regression_cases.wrong_result_seen: 8 to 10 print colours (6 were fabric), inked area 84.9%, black screen at 73.5%, base white at 89.2%, CMYK + whites (6 screens) recommended.

expected.inked_area: only the logo (about 13% of the whole photo in the device test)
